# The fungal world

> *Fungi are eukaryotes with a rigid wall. Most live in soil or on decaying matter, and those that cause human disease are mainly opportunists that take advantage of weakened defences.*

## The six questions, answered for this part {.unnumbered}

| Question | Answer for this kind of microbe |
|---|---|
| What is it built from? | A eukaryotic cell with a wall of chitin and glucan and ergosterol in its membrane; single-celled yeasts or branching moulds |
| How does it get energy, and what does it need to grow? | Its own metabolism, absorbing nutrients from its surroundings; many grow best below body temperature |
| How does it copy itself and change? | Budding in yeasts, spores in moulds |
| Where does it live, and how does it spread? | Soil, plants and decaying matter, from which spores are inhaled; some yeasts live on the body |
| How does damage happen? | Mainly invasion when defences fail; also allergy |
| What does it have that my cells lack? | Ergosterol and the fungal wall: the main targets of antifungal drugs |
